## Landed semantics

- The compiled world's mutable-variable cell holds `fortress.AnyType.Any`, the language's top type, not `runtimeValues.FValue`: `FValue` is an abstract class (`runtimeValues/FValue.java:13`) and a compiled closure is not one of its subclasses, so a mutable variable of arrow type failed the verifier. The defect was already in the tree for *local* mutable variables, which have always been stored in such a cell (`compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static/probes/P15LocalArrow.fss`, `P16LocalArrowTask.fss`: `VerifyError` on `49ee5e91`, `f(1) = 3` after R1), and R1 fixed both kinds by widening the payload (`runtimeValues/MutableFValue.java:18-32`, `runtimeSystem/Transaction.java:20,27-28,144,152,226`).
- **A numeral's value reaches the compiled world intact as of the repair batch of 2026-09-18.** `CodeGen.forIntLiteralExpr` chose the numeral's representation by `BigInteger.bitLength()` against `<= 32` and `<= 64`; `bitLength()` counts no sign bit, so a non-negative numeral of bit length exactly 32 or exactly 64 was truncated into a signed slot and arrived wrapped negative — `4294967295` and `18446744073709551615` both became `-1`, against `Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:83-86` (a numeral of digits has the value of its digits in radix ten, with nothing bounding it) and `basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:368-370,398-401` (wrapping and saturating have their own operator spellings and "operations on type $\mathbb{Z}$ never need to wrap or saturate"). The bounds are now `<= 31` and `<= 63`, exact for both signs, and `FIntLiteral.asNN64` reads the decimal string a numeral of bit length 64 now keeps. Where the compiled run contradicted `walk` in silence it now agrees with it: `4294967295` at `ZZ` prints `4294967295` on both paths, and `a = 4294967295; b = 1; println (a + b)` prints `4294967296` on both (ledger row 317, `compile-ladder/repair-r2-literal-wrap/REPORT.md`).
- **The repair turns one loud failure into a quiet value, and the value it prints is wrong even though the value it holds is right.** `FIntLiteral.asNN64` threw for every string-carried numeral before this rung, and `simpleIntLiteralArith.fromBigInteger` sends every `IntLiteral` arithmetic result of bit length 64 or more to the string branch (`nativeHelpers/simpleIntLiteralArith.java:31-32`), a path R2 does not touch — so the transition needs no numeral of bit length 64 in the source at all. `x = 9223372036854775807` then `n: NN64 = x + x + 1` raised `Error: Not in range for NN64: 18446744073709551615` before R2 and now computes $2^{64}-1$, which `literals.tex:83-86` makes the correct value, and prints it as `-1` because `FNN64.toString` is signed (`compiler/runtimeValues/FNN64.java:20`, ledger row 326). The probe is `compile-ladder/repair-r2-literal-wrap/probes/skeptic/s3.fss` with `s3.compiled` and `s3.walk`; `walk` refuses the coercion instead ("RHS expression type Long is not assignable to LHS type NN64"). ## The library's arrays and algebra

- **Route A's generic container obligations still need body-level checks** (source review, 2026-09-26, `reviews/numeric-hierarchy-integration-review.md`, baseline `c5eada1b2`; measured by climb batch 6 rung F, `d846e3644`, `compile-ladder/rung-flat-tower/REPORT.md` sections 12 and 13). `Vector` and `Matrix` promise scalar results of `T`. On the flat library every operation of `Vector`, `Matrix` and the scalar-extension block runs under `walk` for all seven number types (the norm with an explicit `asFloat`), except `matrix(v)` for `NN32` and `NN64`, because its numeral `0` reaches `T` by coercion; the checker refuses the generic bodies' arithmetic at `(T, T)` ("Could not check call to operator juxtaposition"), where on the nested library it typed it as `RR64` against a declared `T`, so a body bounded only by `T extends Number` still has no evidence for its arithmetic: the obligation is unchanged, its message is not. Row 388 has a concrete integration consequence to test: fixed-receiver `m.scale(i)` against the generic operator `m i`, because only the latter infers the operator's element type and sizes; their divergence is a source prediction, not a matrix probe result. Empty reductions need their advertised result type as well as their identity value. The review proposes bounded checks for the rungs; it takes no new design decision.

- `Vector[\T extends Number, nat s0\]` and `Matrix[\T extends Number, nat s0, nat s1\]` are the only sized array traits; `Array3[\T, nat b0, nat s0, …\]` carries no algebraic trait (row 292; `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1526`, `:1644`, `:1718`).
- `Vector` and `Matrix` inherit `+`, `-`, unary `-` and `zero` from `AdditiveGroup`, nothing else; `×` reaches no array by design because juxtaposition is the inner product and the array traits exclude `AnyMultiplicativeRing` (rows 64, 109, 293); a carrier that extends the ring is accepted unchecked, changes juxtaposition to elementwise and breaks `+` (vocabulary review v02, v02b).
- The library's products are declared with shared `nat`s (`Matrix[\T,n,m\]` × `Matrix[\T,m,p\]`, `FortressLibrary.fsi:1508-1516`); C4's own products were not, which is habit; the focused base's `FlatArrays2` states them (twelve declarations including the per-rank elementwise `×` and `/`, 25 of 29 nats agreeing; 39 declarations), and a wrong-shape call is refused at dispatch, uncatchable for an overloaded name (row 83), as a unification error naming the nat for an unoverloaded one (`apl/mg/checks/mismatch_probe.out`).
- Two declarations of one name differing only in the element type, or a rank-specialised declaration beside an index-generic one, are refused at load ("at least one pair of parameters must have excluding types"; `apl/mg/checks/model_run.out.0`, `elemwise_nat_probe.out.0`); two apis' overloads of one name are checked as one family, so two vocabularies cannot stand in one component (`diag_fwd_two_vocabularies_rejected.out.0`).
- The shipped `RR64` does not satisfy the specification's algebraic bound `T extends AdditiveGroup[\T\]` (vocabulary review, probe `v04b_groupbound.out.0`), as the tower stood before climb batch 6 rung F; on the flat library it does: `RR64` extends `AdditiveGroup[\RR64\]` and `MultiplicativeRing[\RR64\]`, and every number type extends `AdditiveGroup` at its own type (`d846e3644`; "The one library's number tower is flat" under Landed semantics). `Vector` and `Matrix` keep `T extends Number` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1526`, `:1644`), the bound that worked for every element type and rank (row 295).
- The library's scalar-extension block for `+ - MIN MAX` over arrays is generic since `02d09a39f` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4574-4584`, `.fsi:2578-2588`); no reshape, plane, gather, outer product or ravel exists in the library (vocabulary review, section A).
- An array is a trait with `get`/`put`; a view is an object implementing it over other storage, the language's own idiom; the library's row slice `m[i,:]` costs 5× a six-line user view; a diagonal as a `Matrix` view costs 13-54× the operator (vocabulary review v20, v07); a subtype of `Matrix` that overrides `mul` gets its specialised product through the library's own operators, which forward to `mul` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2627-2633`), at the operator's cost and with no api line, since the interpreter dispatches the method on the receiver's run-time type (2026-09-25, `run-c4/probes/vocabulary/diag-override.md`; ledger row 299).

## The specification and the repository's lineage

- **Citing `Specification/library/apis/*.tex` as an independent standard is circular.** `Specification/library/structure.tex:25-31` says in the team's own words that Part Library "is largely automatically generated from the API code for the libraries themselves" and that the libraries are "presently in a state of flux", so `library/apis/CompilerBuiltin.tex` is a rendering of `CompilerBuiltin.fsi` and cannot justify an edit to that same file. Two rung reports cited it as the published api or the spec's shape. The prose chapters of `Specification/basic/` and `basic-lib/` are the standard; the api renderings are not. Sharper still (2026-09-19, batch 1's record worker): the rendered `library/apis/*.tex` files are not in the tree at all, they are generated at spec-build time from the `.fsi` sources (`Specification/library/default-libraries.tex:27,39`), so the `(api listing)` citations of ledger rows 314 and 316 and of `library_tests/IntLiteralArithRung7.fss:30-31` name paths that cannot be opened; the `(api listing)` convention should cite the `.fsi` line instead. Source: the conformance review of the eight rungs, 2026-09-17, `reviews/rung-conformance-1-4.md` and `-5-8.md`, verified in that session.
- The in-repo `Specification/` is the later draft with the implementers' notes, and the one prose to search: `Specification-1.0-frozen/` is the same working draft of 2011-02-02 without the revival's revisions (next entry), and only `fortress.1.0.pdf` beside its sources is the 1.0 artefact, 262 pages, against the draft's 621 since climb batch 6 ("The specification's number chapters describe the flat library" below; `map/spec-to-implementation.md` §1.2).
- **`Specification-1.0-frozen/` is byte for byte the working draft of 2011-02-02, not the 1.0 text, and the specification's own change machinery is unused** (2026-09-26, `reviews/spec-change-form.md`): `git diff --quiet 2f8b4331a:Specification c02fa44d0:Specification-1.0-frozen` succeeds (`2f8b4331a`, 2011-02-02, copyright notices), and nothing changed it since; the team's last change to the text itself is `44e03b176` (2010-12-09). The team left the changes appendix (Appendix I) a stub whose only content is a dead link (`Specification-1.0-frozen/appendices/changes.tex:12-16`), and since climb batch 5 rung S it holds the revival's changes ("The specification states instantiation exclusion" below); the 230 `\note` draft boxes (`fortress.tex:58-62`) print in the committed PDF, which is a draft build; a release build (`\ifrelease`, `fortress.tex:24-29`) has never been made and would also drop the 54 notes that record what is not yet implemented.
- `palimondo/fortress` is a 2018 GitHub fork of `sirinath/fortress`, a git conversion of the project's java.net Mercurial repository: 5,397 trunk commits, root `72ae6881b` (2007-01-04), tip `a874948ac` (2012-08-31), twelve relic branches, the `1.0` tag; the conversion cut 146 parent links (`research/authorship.md:14-22`). The third-party Java 9 port is one squashed commit (`eab48aa6d`) sharing no history with this tree; `8fe1daa8f` (2026-08-18) copied 1,506 of its files onto `a874948ac`, most of it since removed or redone; `clean-ladder` (`8332bd34f`) is a rebuild on `a874948ac` with no graft that never replaced `main`, so `main` still descends from `8fe1daa8f` (the work went on pushing the grafted line to `main` after the rebuild, no rename or merge ever happened) and its tree owes the port one running piece, the `FTypeArrayList` fix for the JDK 8 `TreeSet` crash (`clean-ladder` fixes it in two lines), plus dead files, cosmetic lines and the habit of tracking the generated sources (verified against `clean-ladder`, `lineage.md`). The files that repeat the older account of this lineage are listed in `lineage.md`.
- **The team's latest word on types and on the exclusion rule is the unfinished restart, not `Specification/`** (2026-09-26, `coordinator/spec-lineage.md` and its coordinator's check): `Documentation/Specification/` was begun 2012-02-20 (Luchangco, `166841592`) and abandoned 2012-05-31 with a 65-page build and mostly skeleton chapters; it was never adopted. Its Types chapter (`Prose/Language/types.tick`, Luchangco, 2012-05-31, `275b90773`) is from-scratch prose written a year and a half after `Specification/`'s last edit. It restates the rule as "instantiation exclusion" (:353-376), with a `\note` giving the stronger imposed form: a trait extending two instantiations must extend an expressible one below both. It adds a `covariant` modifier on trait static parameters (:320-339), where the older draft expresses covariance with a self-extending `where` clause (`trait-parameters.tex:339-352`). And it says `Bottom` is inexpressible (:173-195). On static parameters, traits, exceptions, components and the numeric library, `Specification/` is the only statement. "July 19, 2012" on our PDF is the date of the parentless import `5a68404fd`, chosen by the revival in `414b790e3`, not a date of any edit. `fortress.1.0.pdf` is the team's own 2008 artefact (`403afbe0b`), and the root `README.md:106-108` calls the directory beside it "the frozen Fortress 1.0 specification", which only the PDF is.
- **The specification states instantiation exclusion, and its refused examples are the library's shapes, except the number chapters and the calculi of Appendix A** (2026-09-26, climb batch 5 rung S, `3924e7ec3`; `compile-ladder/rung-spec-route-a/decision-record.md`). The rule is stated once, in the later Types chapter's two parts: as a property of exclusion, "Two instantiations of the same parameterized trait exclude each other unless each static argument of one, other than an operator argument, is the same as the corresponding static argument of the other" (`Specification/basic/types-vals-vars.tex:218-237`), and as a rule on declarations beside `InclusiveMolecule` (`basic/traits.tex:299-313`); a where-clause variable may not appear as a static argument in an `extends` clause (`basic/trait-parameters.tex:339-349`). The where-clause section's three declarations, `Nothing` and `Object`'s algebraic clause are kept marked "Not allowed", each with the library's shape beside it: the widening function `widen[\T, S extends T\]`, `object Empty[\T\] extends List[\T\]`, `value object Nothing[\T\] extends Maybe[\T\]` with the exception defaults `Nothing[\String\]` and `Nothing[\Exception\]`, `trait Object extends Any`; the new examples run on both paths as printed, except the specification's `Nothing[\String\]` itself, which the compiled prelude refuses until the switch-over (row 331) (`compile-ladder/rung-spec-route-a/probes/examples/`). Each changed passage carries a `\revision` callout that prints in both builds, and Appendix I has a section "Changes Made by the 2026 Revival to the Working Draft" with the original text of every change cited in `Specification-1.0-frozen/` and route C (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex`, section I.1, from `:18`); the callouts, the appendix and the front matter say that the compiled checker enforces the rule for type arguments and numerals, and the appendix names the cases it does not yet refuse, boolean arguments (row 406) and a static parameter against another argument (row 414), as the merged-diff review's repair corrected them (`compile-ladder/climb-batch-5/JUDGE-review.md`). The three number chapters were left for the flattening and are revised by climb batch 6 rung T (the next entry). Each of the four calculi of Appendix A carries a `\revision` callout saying that it predates the rule and naming the shape it admits (Core Fortress with Where Clauses types a where-clause variable in a supertype, ACFFD admits a self-extension at the parameter's bound, Basic Core claims its programs are all valid Fortress, Core Fortress with Overloading admits Basic Core's shape), its rules and soundness claims unchanged, and Appendix I's entry "The calculi" says so (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex:368-434`), by Pavol's decision (POSITIONS 2026-09-26, the entry on rung S's stop, option 1 of the decision record's section 4.2), landed in `eb2d7e1e6` for the first three and in `09d8dd4a1` for Core Fortress with Overloading; the specification then built to 611 pages (`compile-ladder/climb-batch-5/followup-calculi/NOTE.md`). The specification builds on the container of 2026-09-26 (nproc 4, Intel Xeon @ 2.10GHz, 2100.000 MHz, OpenJDK 25.0.4, `FORTRESS_THREADS=1`, load at start 0.75 to 8.18 across the six runs): `./ant genSource` 44 to 54 s, `./ant tex` 38 to 44 s, 600 pages at `6030e4b36` and 610 after; the committed PDF of 2026-08-23 differed from the base build in Part IV, which is rendered from the library's `.fsi` files, and in one margin note that moved (`compile-ladder/rung-spec-route-a/probes/build/committed-vs-base-pdftotext-diff.txt:193-196`); build logs under `compile-ladder/rung-spec-route-a/probes/build/`, the last pair `gather-genSource.txt` and `gather-tex.txt`.
- **The specification's number chapters describe the flat library, and its advanced chapter on rational quantities is kept word for word as a superseded design** (climb batch 6 rung T, `d9c415395`; `compile-ladder/rung-spec-numbers/decision-record.md`). ℤ, ℤ64, ℤ32, ℕ64, ℕ32, ℚ and ℝ64 are siblings under `Number`, each a subtype of `Number` and none of another, with rung F's coercions: ℚ from the five integer types, ℝ64 from ℤ32 and integer numerals (answer 8's words), ℤ64 from ℤ32 and ℕ32, ℕ64 from ℕ32, ℤ from the four fixed widths, every other conversion explicit, the one into ℝ64 written `asFloat(x)` with the method the one library declares on `Number` (named at the gather, `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:279`) (`Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex:27-49`, `Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:16-37`). The eighteen refined rational types and twelve refined integer types are gone: a subset is tested at run time, and the library's two checks are stated on ℝ64, `getter check(): Maybe[\RR64\]` and `getter check_star(): Maybe[\RR64\]` (`numbers.tex:51-65`). ℚ holds +∞, −∞ and 0/0, as the library's `Ratio` does (measured under walk, `compile-ladder/rung-spec-numbers/probes/examples/RatValues.walk.txt:3-10`) and as the operator chapter says of rational division by zero (`Specification/basic/operators/opr-overview.tex:166`), so its listing no longer claims a field or a total order; the integer types hold no infinity. Answer 7's note is a callout at `Specification/basic/expressions/reductions.tex:27-44`, scoped to the libraries the specification describes, with the compiled path's own smaller library, whose big operators take no static argument, named beside it; answer 8's interim rule, that a generic call or range over two integer types writes its static argument until the promotion rule is written with its implementation, is a callout at `basic-integers.tex:51-65`; the automatic integer-to-float coercion is that of ℤ32 values and of integer numerals to ℝ64, and the coercion chapter's Example 1, a decimal integer literal for a floating-point parameter, stands (`Specification/basic/conversions-coercions.tex:64-69`, `:158-159`). The integer `^` takes a ℤ exponent, and the chapter does not give the result of a negative power, which the Working Draft gave as a rational through ℚ (the callout at `basic-integers.tex:269-291`). Appendix I's entries I.1.10 to I.1.16 quote every original from the Working Draft of February 2011. The rung's own build has 620 pages; the gather checked the chapters against the landed library (`compile-ladder/climb-batch-6/RECORD.md`, rung T) and rebuilt the PDF on the merged tree, 621 pages (`compile-ladder/rung-spec-numbers/probes/build/gather-tex.txt`).
- **The specification never wrote static-argument inference, a numeral's type hierarchy or a range's integer width** (2026-09-27, `reviews/numerics-plan-coordinator/evidence-B.md` §§ 1-2, read; `measure-C.md` § 3). The chapter that the overloading rules (`Specification/basic/overloading.tex:170-175`, static parameters "inferred as described in \chapref{type-inference} before checking the applicability"), `basic/expressions/var-ref.tex:35-40` and `method-invocation.tex:49-52` cite, `Specification/basic/inference.tex`, is 27 lines of heading and notes, one of them "Do we want to forbid such cases where type inference infers BottomTypes for static parameters?" (`:24-25`); the revival's promotion rule (`basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:61-65`), `Empty`'s note (`basic/trait-parameters.tex:478-485`) and the reductions callout (`basic/expressions/reductions.tex:27-44`) point into it. A numeral has a type of its own whose relation to the number types is a note ("We need to describe the Numeral type hierarchy", `basic/expressions/literals.tex:87-96`), and "Libraries define coercions from numerals to integers (for simple numerals) and rational numbers (for compound numerals)" (`:146-148`). The coercion chapter defines applicability with coercion by substitutability and names no static parameter (`basic/conversions-coercions.tex:417-432`), states that "types named by type parameters do not have coercions" (`:363-365`), and uses the expected type to re-choose a declaration only in widening (`:806-848`), which is "not yet supported" (`:15`). The ranges section speaks of "integer values" and names no integer type or width (`basic/expressions/ranges.tex:37-44`), while the draft's own examples build `ZZ64` and `ZZ` ranges ("The cheap fixes and scalar ranges over `ZZ32`, measured on one library copy" above). The later restart adds nothing on these: its Types chapter never says "infer" and its ranges section is a heading (`Documentation/Specification/Prose/Language/types.tick`, `Documentation/Specification/Prose/Language/Expressions/ranges.tick:12`).

## The territory map

- Tasks and transactions are implemented twice, `interpreter/evaluator/` and `runtimeSystem/`, independently (B.11). Row 302's fix is in the compiled world's copy only.
- `import java` also works on the interpreter path through `ForeignComponentWrapper` + `ClosureMaker`, as `map/modules-and-phases.md:451` (B.12) reads it, and it does not: it is wired and unfinished, and no test uses it (`perf-probes/prelude/import-java-interpreter.md`, 2026-09-20). Four gaps, all on the interpreter's side: `NamingCzar.fortLib` is fixed to the builtin api, which declares none of `ZZ32`/`RR64`/`JavaString` in that world (`NamingCzar.java:294-295`); a second `import java` from one package falls through `Driver.ensureApiImplemented` to a `ClassCastException` (`Driver.java:464-466`, "temp hack till we knit in natives properly"); the foreign name is never rewritten (`ForeignComponentWrapper.java:31,38`) and `BaseEnv.java:531-533` bugs on the qualified reference; and `ClosureMaker` emits a call into the compiler's `nativewrapper_cache`, which the interpreter neither writes nor loads. So one binding file cannot serve both worlds; the one-library variant is one shared text with one small builtin component per world behind a single api, which makes the api-to-differently-named-component link (ledger row 320's class-name half, `Linker.whoIsImplementingMyAPI`) live work.
- Codegen refuses any declaration carrying a where clause or a contract (`CodeGen.java:2953`/`:2957` in `forFnDecl`, `:4093`/`:4095` in `forObjectDeclPrePass`, `:5004`/`:5006` in `forTraitDecl`); not in the ledger (flagged, Pavol's call). `atomic <expr>` has no visitor, `atomic do … end` compiles; `spawn`, `label`/`exit`, object expressions, array literals and comprehensions, local function declarations have no visitor (`spec-to-implementation.md` §3).
- The checker (`IndexBuilder.scala:187-189`) refuses `type` aliases, `test` and `property` on both paths. Coercion, which the compiler path had and the interpreter did not (row 19), converts on both paths since climb batch 4 rung C (`b628871a2`; "Under `walk`, the interpreter converts by coercion at its three kinds of type check" under Landed semantics).
- **The compiled path's only array-like types are `ZZ32Vector` and `StringVector`, two hand-written Java classes declared only in its prelude and absent from the specification** (2026-09-25, `compiler-probes/vectors/vectors.md`, probes and captures under `compiler-probes/vectors/probes/`). `FZZ32Vector` holds an unboxed `int[]` with lower bounds and an optional second dimension (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/runtimeValues/FZZ32Vector.java:14-19`), `FStringVector` a `String[]`; `NamingCzar`'s special table lowers both types straight to the classes (`compiler/NamingCzar.java:553-554`); every element access is boxed and passes through seven frames, a generated native wrapper among them; no gated test creates or indexes a `ZZ32Vector` at run time. The load failure of a `ZZ32Vector` passed to a generic object's constructor (ledger row 408, expected failure `compiler_tests/XXXVecCtorLoad`) is the descriptor class's name: both classes call it `RTTIv` (`FZZ32Vector.java:79-82`) while stamped code asks for `<class>$RTTIc` (`runtimeSystem/MethodInstantiater.java:134-138`), and a probe-only copy with an `RTTIc` alias runs (`probes/rttic-alias.patch`, `out-VecGeneric-rttic.txt`). A native helper cannot take a Java array: the wrapper generator skips every method with an array parameter (`compiler/nativeInterface/SignatureParser.java:45-55`). Written by Christine Flood (`f4973a717`, `24717d4ad`, 2011) and extended by Guy Steele (`d535963cb`, 2011-10-12).
- **A generic object referenced without its static arguments is a static error on the compiled path, and the checker never consults the expected type for it** (2026-09-19, `explorations/compiler-probes/maybe-inference/inference.md`): `b: Box[\ZZ32\] = Box` fails with `Ill-formed type: Box`; a bare `Empty` as a call argument or a field default fails with `T is not in the kind env`, an internal `bug()` from `TypeAnalyzer.scala:766` reported at the declaration's span; the same forms with the static argument written compile and run on both paths. The decision is in the checker's `SVarRef` case, `typechecker/impls/Misc.scala:624-641`, whose `:639-640` keeps the uninstantiated type under the team's own `TODO: handle missing static args`; static-argument inference exists only for arrows (`STypesUtil.scala:912-930`, called from application and coercion), and a parametric empty case reached by `coerce` still fails bare. Under `walk` the same forms are `InterpreterBug: Couldn't figure out Empty[\T\](uninstantiated) <: Opt[\ZZ32\]`. Consequence for row 331: a parametric `Nothing[\T\]` would serve the corpus's `Nothing[\ZZ32\]` and never the specification's bare `= Nothing`; the non-parametric object plus `coerce` that the prelude uses is the only shape that compiles, so `Maybe` stays as landed. Incidental, row 340: a `typecase` used directly as a function or method body whose value needs an implicit coercion (`IntLiteral` to a declared `ZZ32`) crashes code generation with `Error trying to close method scope`, because ASM's stack-map frame computation fails (`ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` under `MethodWriter.visitMaxs`, relabelled by the `catch (Throwable)` at `CodeGen.java:2806-2807`); neither a generic object nor `typecase` alone is the trigger (the minimal reproducer, `compiler-probes/maybe-inference/probes/TcPlain.fss`); wrapped in `do … end` the same body compiles, and every gated use of the shape returns `()` so never reaches the coercion.
- The gate: two corpora, hand-ported: `tests/` shares no file name with `compiler_tests/`, and the 11 names it shares with `other_compiler_tests/` are different programs; only `parser_tests/` is read by both suites, and no test compares the paths on one program (`map/README.md`); interpreter tests pass on "no exception and no `fail` in output" (`FileTests.java:367-371`), compiler run tests on exit code plus `PASS`. `fortress.unittests.noopt=true` (`default_repository/configuration:51`) hides 283 tests and leaves the 43-file bytecode optimizer with zero (`map/README.md`, re-measured 2026-09-27). Every `testSystem` shard and every `testFast` fork runs `FORTRESS_THREADS=1` (`build.xml:1188`, `:947`), so no suite test sees concurrency and the gate's four-thread `atomic` runs are its one concurrent check; `TransactionJUTest`'s multi-threaded half is commented out (`TestTask.java:43-44`). `nat`-parameterised programs are compiled and run since climb batches 4 and 5 (`compiler_tests/Nat*`); the cache round trip is not asserted (`ASTJUTest.java:654`). 121 `.fss` inside green directories are dark; `linker_tests`, `compiler_regressions`, `BirdyLib`, the `not_working_*` directories are orphaned (`map/test-coverage.md`).

content.content:
## The container

- The process cost of the climbs and the batches — the eight-rung climb's wall clock and its gate share, the limits of parallelism on this box, and each batch's agents, tokens, tool calls and span — is measured in `explorations/coordinator/iteration-cost.md`, `coordinator/repair-batch-review.md` and the batch records; the conclusions it produced are in `POSITIONS.md` and in `coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js`, and the entries themselves are in `FACTS-history.md`.
- The Bash tool's 10-minute ceiling kills long runs; check runs go under the `Monitor` tool (1800000 ms), sequential, nothing else running when a number is to be kept.
- The disk allowance fills with parser-generation temp directories: every run that imports a grammar generates a Rats! parser into a fresh `/tmp/fortress<random>rats` directory (`RatsUtil.getTempDir`, `syntax_abstractions/rats/RatsUtil.java:138-146`, via `IOUtil.createAndMarkTempDirectory`), 5.8 MB each, never deleted; 723 of them (4.2 GB) filled the allowance on 2026-09-15 and broke a worker's tool output mid-run ("no space left on device"). Deficit until fixed at the source (an edit to the original tree, or a `deleteOnExit`); mitigation in our tree: `explorations/experiment/env.sh` removes them when sourced, and `df` must be checked before any long run.
- A container can be lost outright: the coordinating session of 2026-09-17 (`bdff267d-…`) died mid-workflow and could not be re-provisioned, because the branch it was created from was no longer found on the remote. Recovery moved into the blinded run's container, which already had the checkout and toolchain. Cost: four workflow agents (~798k tokens), their worktrees, and the 13 hours after the last transcript snapshot at 20:31. Everything through `2ab1d6d8` was pushed and safe, and `REPAIR-BATCH.md` kept the batch runnable. Mechanism, the three traps and the recovery procedure: `explorations/coordinator/remote-container.md`.
- The transcript backup fires on the main session's Stop, not on any agent's completion, and swallows all errors: a session inside one long turn is not being backed up and a failed push is silent. Workflow-agent transcripts were outside its globs until 2026-09-18; oversized transcripts now split at 64 MiB, and the wrapper packs loose objects because the clone ships `gc.auto=0`.
- **The Workflow harness runs two agents at once on this box** (measured 2026-09-18, four one-command agents in one `parallel()`: agents 0 and 1 started 19:14:08, agents 2 and 3 at 19:14:31 after the first pair finished at 19:14:23; `batched-climb-plan.md` §2). `model: 'opus'` in `agent()` resolves to a fixed model identifier, readable in each agent transcript's `message.model` field and not written here (the protocol's hard rule that no model identifier is committed); an agent with no `model` inherits the session's. A subagent's floor is about 45k tokens before it does anything (183k for the four). Prompt caching across parallel agents covers the system prompt and tools only (33,022 tokens read by agents 1–3) and not the first user message (11,010 written by each), because a cache read lands only at a breakpoint the harness placed and a shared prefix inside one message is not one.
- The VM can be restarted under a live session with the disk intact: 2026-09-18 23:22 UTC, 25 minutes into the repair batch's re-run, kernel build string fc-v33 → fc-v37, one JVM running (16 GB, no swap, 4 CPUs: not a memory death). Worktrees, uncommitted edits and agent transcripts survived; the Workflow run and its agents did not, and the run was relaunched from its base (a resume of its finished agents was not tried; see the entry on 2026-09-27 below); the `wip/` branches held every pushed milestone (`remote-container.md` § The 2026-09-18 restart).
- **A user interrupt of the coordinating session's turn kills a background Workflow run** (2026-09-19): climb batch 1's first run, `wf_a29fd04b-a9a`, launched 07:15 UTC, lost both its rung agents at 07:46:42, when an interrupt cut the turn that a check-in trigger had just started; both agent transcripts end at that second, no result line reached the journal, and the harness no longer knew the task. Rung F had written its closing text at 07:45:41 without returning its result, so only M was mid-work. No message caused the death: none was enqueued between the check-in at 07:46:30 and Pavol's next message at 07:48:34, and at 09:05 he said he had pressed nothing. The `wip/` branches held F's three and M's three milestones and M's worktree its uncommitted report, so the relaunch at 08:25 from the same base continued under the prefix's continuation clause. Cost: about 40 minutes of two workers. The batch was relaunched after that death (a resume was not tried then; the entry on 2026-09-27 below); the rule for every turn is the entry "Stopping a turn kills every background agent alive at that moment" below (session `fe616d40`, main transcript and `subagents/`).
- **A message from Pavol that arrives while the coordinator is inside a turn kills a running Workflow's agents, whatever the turn is doing**: this reading of the death of 2026-09-26 is wrong, and the death was an interrupt, as on 09-19. Batch 5's run `wf_eb47c103-304`, launched 11:10 UTC, lost both rung agents at 12:07:47 UTC, inside a turn that was recording a decision, not a check-in: both transcripts end at that second with "[Request interrupted by user for tool use]", the journal stops at their two `started` lines, and the harness no longer knows the task (`TaskStop` finds no such task). The turn's pending Bash is recorded "User rejected tool use" at 12:07:47.797 and "[Request interrupted by user]" at .799; no message was enqueued between "Yes, agreed." (12:07:33, already delivered) and the next one at 12:08:32; at 12:09 Pavol asked whether he had pressed stop by accident and at 12:10 named the iOS stop button under his right thumb. A message sent during a turn is queued, not an interrupt: it is delivered inside the turn (16:13:08 the same day, with `wf_88172730-ebe` working on) or as the next turn, and eleven such messages during live runs from 09-19 to 09-26 killed none, so the advice at the launch, that messages are safe, was right. What survived: rung Z's three pushed commits and rung D's one, with their worktrees' uncommitted files, and rung D's orphaned count run (session `fe616d40`, main transcript 12:07:33-12:10:46 and 16:13:08; `subagents/workflows/wf_eb47c103-304/`).
- **A manual compaction issued between turns leaves a running Workflow alive** (found 2026-09-19 by a worker in the archived transcript of session `bdff267d`, `transcripts` branch, parts file `001.jsonl`): the eight-rung climb's run `wf_73833dfb-d25` (launched 2026-09-17 06:00:57 UTC) survived two `/compact` commands, boundaries 10:47:33 (442,504 tokens before, 130 s) and 14:25:25 (177,831 tokens, 153 s), both typed while the session sat between turns; rung 5's commit landed 84 s after the first boundary, rungs 6-8 and the final re-run followed, and the run's completion notification arrived 14:39:09 with all eight rungs. In this container three manual compactions fell inside live runs, 09-19 09:47 (`wf_3b5a273c-a80`), 09-20 05:32 (`wf_d1628adb-2ee`) and 09-26 12:26 (`wf_88172730-ebe`), and each run's agents kept writing through the compaction (40 to 66 records inside its window) and went on to their results (session `fe616d40`, `subagents/workflows/`); its compactions of 09-18 18:38 and 22:54 and 09-19 06:38 coincided with no run. The 09-19 death was a mid-turn interrupt, not a compaction; the rule is the entry below.
- **Stopping a turn kills every background agent alive at that moment; a message sent while the coordinator is busy kills nothing** (2026-09-26, `coordinator/interrupt-archaeology/judgement.md` § 1, from `coordinator/interrupt-archaeology/evidence.md`; session `fe616d40`, main transcript, `subagents/` and `subagents/workflows/`; session `bdff267d`, `transcripts` branch, `001.jsonl`). The kill is the turn interrupt the transcript records as "[Request interrupted by user]", with any tool still in flight recorded "User rejected tool use": in the four interrupts that met live background agents (2026-09-19 07:46:42, 09-22 07:18:51, 09-25 22:31:59, 09-26 12:07:47) all seven agents alive died at that instant, Workflow agents and `Agent`-tool workers alike, and none ever survived one. Eleven messages and three `/context` commands sent while the coordinator was busy, during five live runs from 09-19 to 09-26, killed nothing: each was queued and delivered inside the running turn or as the next turn. Five manual compactions between turns killed nothing either (09-17 10:47 and 14:25, 09-19 09:47, 09-20 05:32, 09-26 12:26). That the stop button sent the interrupt is confirmed for 09-25 in Pavol's words and very likely for 09-26 (the iOS client's stop control under his right thumb), not shown for 09-19; the transcripts record the effect, not the control. Not tested: an automatic compaction mid-turn, and an interrupt during the Stop hook while a run is alive. The rule: send messages at any time; compact between turns; do not stop a turn while the session is working, including the seconds after a reply while the transcript backup runs; after an accidental stop, say so and the run is resumed with `resumeFromRunId`, which keeps every agent that had finished (the entry on 2026-09-27 below; POSITIONS 2026-09-26, the interrupt ruling). The three entries above are the incidents it rests on.
- **A restart of the session's own process kills its background runs, and `resumeFromRunId` then recovers every agent that had finished** (2026-09-27, session `fe616d40`). At 12:09:17 UTC the environment manager restarted the session's Claude Code process (`environment-manager task-run … --session-mode resume`; the VM itself was not restarted, `uptime -s` still 2026-09-26 23:11:31, kernel fc-v37); the cause is not visible from inside. Batch 6b's run `wf_08949b8a-a21` and an `Agent`-tool worker died with it: the run's repair agent's transcript ends 12:09, four minutes into its stage. The conversation, worktrees, untracked files and transcripts survived. A relaunch from the base (12:12, `wf_2da3e152-2d5`) restarted at the first stage; the same script and arguments with `resumeFromRunId: wf_08949b8a-a21` (12:20) took rung O's worker, skeptic and judge from the old run's `journal.jsonl` without running them (the journal keys match when the script text and arguments are identical) and started the repair stage anew. So after a death that leaves the session, its ID and the run's journal in place, the run is resumed with the same script text, not relaunched; a finished agent's result is kept, an unfinished one runs from its start, and its worktree's leftovers are its starting point. A run whose script has changed since launch is resumed from a copy of the script as launched (`git show <base>:<path>`). What does not carry over is a new session: `remote-container.md` § The 2026-09-18 restart and step 5 of the recovery list. The same restart undid a compaction: the resumed process rebuilt the conversation from the transcript as if the manual compaction of 08:40 had not happened, from the one of 03:28 on, so the context the model saw went from 421K on the last call before the restart to 802K on the first after it with nothing new in the chat, and the automatic compaction fired at 12:11 at 805K. Measured: the 12:11 boundary's `cumulativeDroppedTokens`, 8,783,976, is the 03:28 boundary's 7,994,881 plus its own 789,095, leaving out the 08:40 compaction's 741,537, and the 03:28 boundary record appears a second time in the transcript at the reload (lines 25826 and 32220); what the reload sent beyond that is inferred, not shown (`explorations/reviews/coordinator-context-2026-09-27.md`, `e15e1a01a`). After a restart of the session's process, `/context` shows whether it happened again.
- **`explorations/experiment/env.sh` is the one script every probe and gate runner sources, and it is verified from its new home** (2026-09-24, after `7bc8177a3` moved `experiment/` under `explorations/`): it derives `FORTRESS_HOME` from its own location two levels up, and re-running the two shadow experiments that source it, `reviews/mie-probes/forest/forest-run.sh` (423 s) and `perf-probes/nat/runtime/run-all.sh` (669 s), reproduced every committed count and probe output (`checker-count.txt`'s six counts, stock 103 and forest 37 among them, and captures r1-r5 byte-identical); the only differences were dates, timings and line numbers shifted by the library commits `c2b4e2c95` and `d6faad28f` made after the captures. astra's scripts keep their own `experiment/` paths, which name astra's tree.
- **A check-in cadence under an hour is a series of one-shot `send_later` check-ins armed together in one turn, not a cron trigger and not a re-armed one-shot** (2026-09-26, a Sonnet worker's search of session `fe616d40`'s main transcript at Pavol's request). The scheduler's cron triggers take an hour as their shortest interval. For batch 5, at 11:10:40-43 UTC, the coordinator made seven `send_later` calls in one turn, each `{"at": ..., "name": "Batch 5 check-in N", "message": ...}`, `at` 12:40 to 17:10 UTC 45 minutes apart; they fired at 12:40:47, 13:25:43, 14:10:41, 14:55:50, 15:40:28, 16:25:54 and 17:10:58, within a minute of each target, with no re-arming. Batch 4's four were 90 minutes apart (01:31 UTC, `at` 03:01 to 07:31), though one of them was relabelled "one of the 45-minute series". Batches 1 to 3 chained one `send_later` per check-in, each re-issued by the turn it started (batch 3 fired seven times at 58-60 minute spacing). The scheduler refuses more than about ten trigger creations a minute: the eleventh `send_later` of batch 6's series, at 23:50:52 UTC, got "Trigger creation rate limit reached. Try again in 56s." A series ends when its last check-in has fired, so a run that outlasts it needs a new series, armed by the last check-in.
- **`agent()` in a Workflow returns null for an agent the harness marks failed, even after the agent delivered its structured output** (2026-09-27, climb batch 6, run `wf_b262c534-337`; `coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.md`, "An agent that comes back with nothing"). At 03:34:03 UTC rung R's second skeptic returned its verdict, an approval with one required correction, through the structured-output tool; the API's safety filter then blocked its next message, a false-positive `reasoning_extraction` refusal, and the harness marked the agent failed (the run's `journal.jsonl`, line 24, `"type":"failed"`). `agent()` returned null, and the script recorded rung R as `dropped`, although that approval is committed on `wip/rung-unknown-size-arm` (`217653909`). Since then every `agent()` call of the batch script goes through `callAgent`, which treats a null or undefined result and a thrown error alike and runs the role up to two more times, each retry told what the earlier attempt may have left (`coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js:1582`, `:1603-1626`).

## The ledger

- Rows are never renumbered or moved, and the reports cite them by number; the counts by kind are derived by script in the ledger's counts (`fortress-gap-ledger.md:783`), and the revival worklist (46 items, `fortress-gap-ledger.md:643`) and `apl/lessons.md` are the two derived views. Five cost rows sit in section 15; whether they get a section of their own is Pavol's call.

<!-- The territory map, assembled 2026-09-16 by the coordinating session from the survey reports in this directory, before the historical source tree was opened for modification. The surveys are the evidence of that day; sections 0, 2 and 7 describe the tree as it stands, section 6 the development loop, and the order of work and the open decisions are in coordinator/PLAN.md, to which sections 4 and 5 point. Every claim cites a survey section, a file:line, a commit, or a FACTS or POSITIONS entry. Read after FACTS.md and POSITIONS.md; it does not repeat them. -->

# The territory map

## 0. Terms used here

Path: one of the two execution routes, the interpreter (`fortress <file>.fss`, "walk") or the compiler (`fortress compile` then `fortress run`); "both paths" means the shared front end.

World: which prelude a run links against; the interpreter world is `FortressLibrary` + `FortressBuiltin` + `AnyType`, the compiler world is `CompilerLibrary` + `CompilerBuiltin` + `CompilerAlgebra` + `AnyType` (`compiler/WellKnownNames.java:114-139`, `CompilerAlgebra` since `1bd8d3ad1`; `modules-and-phases.md` B.13).

Prelude: the library a world loads without an import; the compiler world's four components are 2,405 lines against the interpreter world's 5,314 (`wc -l` of the `.fss`; `spec-to-implementation.md` §2 names the files).

Switch-over: phase 4 of `coordinator/PLAN.md`, where the compiled path starts reading the interpreter's library and the compiler's own three prelude files are deleted, their tests kept (POSITIONS 2026-09-21, the library route); until then each path links its own world.

Gate: what a change must pass to land: on a clean build, `ant testFast` and `ant testSystem` at zero failures, thirteen compiled `atomic` programs three times at four threads, the ladder regression (85 files compiled and run against their baseline, the eighteen microGPT components compiled only) and the checker count, the compiled checker's errors over the interpreter's library, reported and never red on its own (protocol, hard rules; `coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.md`). Counts here are from climb batch 5's follow-up D gate (`compile-ladder/climb-batch-5/followup-D/gate/summary.txt`); the c

Shadow: a prototype of an edit to the original tree, made by compiling edited copies of the files and putting their class files ahead of the real ones on the classpath; no tracked file changes, and the gate cannot see it (`perf-probes/template-check/run-all.sh`; FACTS "The `nat` plan's minimal design works as a shadow").

Sealed tree: the original tree, everything outside `explorations/` and `research/`; sealed through `75cca6683` (POSITIONS 2026-09-17), editable since, each edit test first and flagged at commit (protocol, hard rules).

## 1. The five surveys, and the walkthrough beside them

`modules-and-phases.md`: the 22 packages with sizes, the import graph, the dead modules, the two pipelines phase by phase, the cache, the runtime, native interop, and the one-table divergence of the paths (B.14).

`spec-to-implementation.md`: the 53 chapters of the July 2012 draft, a table of about 110 features with the parser rule, checker class, interpreter, codegen and prelude location of each, and the layered picture of the numeric tower (§4).

`test-coverage.md`: the census of every test corpus and JUnit class, what the 1,377 and 382 are made of, the two corpora that never meet, the blind spots by module, and the loop timings.

`dormant-code.md` (part five, added at Pavol's request): the census of what is present, carries a design, and does not run: commented-out library declarations and `Library/incomplete/`, commented-out visitors and off-by-default flags in the source, commented-out test halves and the aspirational directories, the spec's genuinely dormant text and its 62 "not yet supported" notes, the papers; each item judged finished-unwired, sketch, superseded or unknown, and tied to a path step.

`design-intent-sources.md`: the five places rationale is written (in-repo papers, the Steele corpus, our extracts, the spec's draft-only notes and Internal Document, source comments and commits), and a table by design area of what intent the spec leaves unstated.

`compile-path-walkthrough.md` (part six, written 2026-09-20 for the checker decisions): the compile path followed end to end, one section per stage — parsing, name resolution and grammar expansion, the checker (what it walks, what it writes, its counts on the library before climb batch 4), the desugaring switches that make the paths differ, code generation, the second JVM and the stamping class loader, native bindings in both worlds, `nat`, and a glossary.

## 2. The shape of the system, in thirteen facts

The editable surface is about 149,000 hand-written Java lines and 19,900 Scala lines; the other 535,000 Java lines are generated and checked in (counted as in `modules-and-phases.md` A.1).

The AST in `nodes/` is the only intermediate representation from parse to bytecode; there is no lower IR and no optimizing middle (B.1).

# Measure C: the cheap fixes on one tree, scalar ranges over ZZ32, and what other integer ranges cost

For the coordinator's plan on the numerics on the path to compilation. This is measurement only and recommends nothing. Gathered 2026-09-27, 16:20 to 17:15 UTC, on `main` at `d7ca74708`. `Library/` and `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/` are byte for byte those of `d65892d34`, the sources the triage ran on (`git diff --quiet d65892d34 HEAD -- Library ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin`). The only source change since then is `917bb7b32`, in the interpreter's natives.

## How to read this

- `C/` means `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-fortress/fe616d40-a9c6-56d7-9da1-7168a172765d/scratchpad/coordinator-plan/probes-C/`, and `W/` means `C/work/`. Every capture and script named below is there.
- [measured] marks a count taken from a run's capture. [read] marks something read from source or text and not run.
- **Line numbers are the tree's.** L0 and tree 1 have the tree's lines, since tree 1 moves no line. Tree 2's locations are carried back to tree 1's lines, except where a location says "in the copy".
- An *error* is one distinct error as `distance-triage/fullerrs.py` counts it, with the whole message. A *site* is an error's kind and location, the n-th error at a line matched with the n-th. This is how `compare.py --sites` counts. Classes are those of `distance-triage/classify.py`, unchanged.
- **Machine for every run.** `nproc` 4; `Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.10GHz`; `cpu MHz` 2100.000; OpenJDK 25.0.4; `FORTRESS_THREADS=1`; `-Xmx4g -Xss64m`.
  - Another worker's runs (`probes-D`, up to eight JVMs) shared the machine from about 16:40.
  - Load average at the start of each run, from the capture's head: L0 1.31 / 1.35, T1 9.31 / 9.37, T2 14.38 / 14.38 (walk / any).
  - Elapsed: L0 927 / 919 s, T1 1,607 / 1,605 s, T2 1,445 / 1,441 s (`W/stage-*.out`, `ELAPSED`).
  - No timing here is a comparison. The counts do not depend on load.

## Method

- **Driver.** `distance-triage/run.sh` step `stage` is used unchanged, through `C/stage.sh`: DistanceMulti over the twelve prelude components of a library copy, every stage and declaration, overload memo off, one private cache per run.
  - `C/stage.sh` adds only `-Djava.io.tmpdir` under `W/`, through run.sh's `EXTRA_FLAGS`.
  - The shadows and drivers were built into `W/` by `run.sh <W> build` (`C/build.log`, `W/make-shadows.txt`). `ant` was not run.
- **The two settings.**
  - Walk's setting is `-setting walk`.
  - The third setting is the flat note's `stage-any`: `switch-over-distance-flat/run-all.sh` runs `DistanceMulti -order check -setting any`, which means the bound `Any` with compiled-expression desugaring on (`DistanceMulti.java` header; flat note § 5). `run.sh stage <v> any` passes the same flag.
- **Library copies.** `C/lib.sh <name> <variant>` copies every `.fsi`/`.fss` of `Library/` and `LibraryBuiltin/` into `W/libs/<name>/`, then runs `C/variants_c.py`.
  - `variants_c.py` calls `distance-triage/variants.py` unchanged for BP, R421, BOUNDS and DEVICE, and adds FAILB and Z32 (below).
  - Every edit asserts its count.
  - The copies are `W/libs/L0` (control), `T1` and `T2`. The diffs are `C/tree1.patch` (L0 to T1, 418 lines) and `C/tree2.patch` (T1 to T2, 3,316 lines).
- **Classification and comparison.**
  - Classes: `classify.py`.
  - Tree 1 against the controls: `compare.py --sites -v`. Tree 1 moves no line, so no line map is needed.
  - Tree 2 against tree 1: `C/compare_c.py`. It is compare.py with two changes. Its line map is taken after a normalisation that forgets static argument lists, the names I, J, K and ZZ32, and spacing. It classifies tree 2's errors at tree 1's lines, because classify.py has four line-range rules (I1, V1, G1) that tree 2's shifted lines would otherwise miss.
  - `C/transitions.py` gives, site by site, what became of each base error (gone, or still an error and in which class) and the new sites. `C/families.py` splits L1 and M1 by family and gives the range parts of M1, OT and NM.
- **Walk.** `C/walk.sh <copy> <Test>` runs `com.sun.fortress.Shell` on `ProjectFortress/tests/<Test>.fss` with `-Dfortress.source.path=;.;<copy>;…/test_library`, a private cache and a private temp directory.
  - The triage's scripts do not put a copy in front of the interpreter; their copies are checker targets only. `explorations/reviews/sum-replacement-judgement/walk-shadow.sh` and `perf-probes/nat/zero/run-all.sh` do, with this property.
  - I checked that the mechanism reaches the copy. A copy with `roundToStride` renamed fails `RangeTest` with "Variable roundToStride is not defined" at the copy's `RangeInternals.fss:39` [measured; the capture was overwritten, and the check is repeatable with `walk.sh`].
- **Controls** [measured]: L0 gives **1,738** under walk's setting and **1,746** under `any` (`W/stage-L0-*.tally.txt`).
  - The triage's L0 walk was 1,738, and my classes match its `classes.txt` except O1 13 against 15 and BR 11 against 9. Those are the run-to-run variation families (`C/classes-L0.txt`).
  - The flat note's single `any` run was 1,747.

## 1. Tree 1: BP, FAILB, R421, BOUNDS, DEVICE

**What is in it** (`C/tree1.patch`; [read] from the diff):
- BP: `builtinPrimitive[\T extends Object\]` in `FortressBuiltin.fsi:30` and `.fss`.
- FAILB: the written bound `Object` on the two result-only static parameters behind N2.
  - `fail[\T extends Object\](s:String):T` at `FortressLibrary.fsi:37` and `.fss:54`. This covers 21 of N2's 24 errors, and `RangeInternals.fss:157`, whose loop fails on the `fail` inside it at `:159`.
  - `opr BIG <|[\T extends Object\]|>` at `List.fsi:109` and `List.fss:177`: the nullary comprehension behind `List.fss:150`.
  - Not changed: N2's `FortressLibrary.fss:169`, `opr >=(self, other:Comparison): Boolean = NOT (other < self)`. Its whole message ends "Could not infer static arguments A, B without context. - Could not infer static arguments A, B, C without context" (`W/full-L0-walk.tsv`). That is the tuple comparisons `opr <[\A,B\]` and `[\A,B,C\]`, whose parameters appear in their argument types. They are not result-only.
- R421: `StandardMinMax`'s `MIN` and `MAX` declared `T`, api and component.
- BOUNDS: the 138 `AnyIntegral` bounds become `Integral[\X\]`, and `RightScalarRange` and `emptyScalarRange` take that bound.
- DEVICE: the 18 operators pass their own first arguments instead of `0 asif ZZ32`.

**Is writing `extends Object` on a static parameter the library's own practice?** [read, by grep] No, not in `Library/` or `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/`.
- The only `extends Object` there is on declarations, not parameters: `String.fsi:25` `object StringStats() extends Object` and `CompilerLibrary.fsi:281` `trait Matrix[\T, nat s0, nat s1\] extends Object`.
- The library writes the bound `Any` instead: `cast`, `instanceOf`, `identity`, `shared`, `localize` and `copy` at `FortressLibrary.fsi:24,26,32,45,49,52`, and throughout `CompilerLibrary.fs?`.
- The specification's examples do write it on static parameters:
  - `SpecData/examples/basic/Fun.Decl.fss:19` `Cons[\T extends Object, nat length\](…)` and `:21`;
  - Fortress source in `Specification/appendices/internal-document.tex:431` `value trait LinearSequence[\T extends Object, nat n\]` and `future.tex:242`;
  - `where` clauses at `basic-lib/convenience.tex:61` and `basic/trait-parameters.tex:359`, `:405`.
- So do compiler tests, e.g. `ProjectFortress/other_compiler_tests/Go1a.fss:15`, `IGO2.fss:26`, `GenMet6.fss:14`.

**Totals** [measured]:
- **Walk's setting: 1,738 → 1,239**. By site, 513 went and 14 appeared (`C/compare-T1-walk.txt`).
- **The `any` setting: 1,746 → 1,253**. By site, 512 went and 19 appeared (`C/compare-T1-any.txt`).
- The same eight declarations crash the checker as in L0 (`W/stage-T1-*.tally.txt`, crash section).

**Per-class moves, walk** (`C/classes-T1.txt`; the sites' fates are in `C/transitions-T1-walk.txt`):
- N1 340 → 0, from BP.
- N2 24 → 1. 22 sites went. `List.fss:150` is now GB, "BottomType->CovariantCollection.AnyCovColl is not applicable…", the message the compile path's setting gives there (digest, part 5, item 9). The one left is `FortressLibrary.fss:169`, above.
- R1 32 → 0 and R4 18 → 4, from R421. OT −4 are row 421's cascades (`List.fss:72`, `:75`, `:332`, `RangeInternals.fss:449`), and TS −1 is `List.fss:320`.
- I1 81 → 4. 69 went, and 8 sites are now I3 (numerals unmasked behind `+`). The 4 left are the unbounded `opr (x:I):[\I\]`, `openRange[\I\]()`, `opr (l:I)::[\I\]` and `opr ::[\I\](l:I,s:I)` (`FortressLibrary.fss:3921`, `:3946`, `:3957`, `:3966`).
- I2 18 → 2. The device's 18 all went. The 2 new are `List.fss:322` and `:333`, `fill` on `ImmutableArray`: the misclassification of the digest's part 5, item 4, unmasked by R421.
- I3 149 → 160: 2 went, 2 are now RG, 8 came from I1, and 7 are new sites (the extent helpers' `-` with a numeral at `RangeInternals.fss:1451`, `:1460`, `:1470`, and `:702`).
- D2 18 → 20: +2 at `RightScalarRange` (`RangeInternals.fss:681`), unmasked by its new bound.
- RG 29 → 31 (+2 from I3); X1 12 → 10 (row 358's two).
- The rest move within the variation families only: OT −2 besides row 421's 4 (`FortressLibrary.fss:1317`, `:1320`, the ranges inferred at `IntLiteral`); V2 42 → 39; BR 11 → 10; O1 13 → 13 (one pair renamed); GB 7 → 8 (N2's).

**Per-class moves, `any`** (`C/classes-T1.txt` columns 3 and 4):
- The same moves as walk's, with D1 12 → 12 (the compiled desugaring's abstract methods), X1 11 → 10, and V2 39 → 41 (3 gone, 5 new, the variation family).

**What rungs A and H would add on top** [read: the digest's reading applied to tree 1's measured class counts; not run]:
- **Rung A, the `fill` rename.** It clears, by the digest's reading (part 2, "7 A"):
  - A1 244 (both settings: under `any`, A1 is 244 in `C/classes-T1.txt`, as the flat note § 5 says);
  - A2 58;
  - R3's `array1`/`array2`/`array3` 5 (2 + 2 + 1, both settings; `W/classes-T1-*.txt`).
  - That is up to **307**.
- **Rung H.** By its brief, H1 38 and H2 2, **40**. By the digest's reading ("7 H") also O1 13, R2's 17 `Unordered` pairs, MB 7 and L1's `CMP` 4, **41 more**, all as counted in tree 1.
- **Arithmetic only.** Tree 1 less rung A and H's brief is walk 1,239 − 347 = 892 and `any` 1,253 − 347 = 906. With H's by-reading families it is 851 and 865. Interactions between the rungs and tree 1 are not measured.
- One interaction [read]: H's keep-the-rule sketch drops `AnyIntegral` from `Integral`'s extends clause (digest, H2). In tree 1, `RangeInternals` and the range operators no longer name `AnyIntegral`: 0 mentions in `RangeInternals.fs?`, down from 21 and 12. `FortressLibrary.fss` and `.fsi` still name it 28 and 20 times outside the range block (grep over `W/libs/T1`).

# measure-D: the expected type kept at a call `f(x)`

Every number names its capture, relative to `probes-D/`. **[measured]** means a run here produced it. **[read]** means it was read from the source and not traced.

## The answers

1. **The shadow.** It is four one-token edits in `Operators.scala`: `, expected` added at `:85`, `:90`, `:197` and `:345` (`shadow-fix.patch`).
   - The line the brief names, `:90`, is not the path of a parsed call. The parser builds `f(x)` as a tight juxtaposition with `fnApp = false`. That goes `:85` → `:345` → `:197`.
   - `:90` alone changes nothing on the probes. The three edits without it (`fixmp`) give the same result as all four **[measured]**.
   - I did not change the other drops of the same kind (§ 1.3): the loose juxtaposition `f x`, arguments, `let` bodies, `if` with no `else`, `typecase`, and `for` bodies.
2. **What `T` becomes.** With the expected type kept, a result-only `T` becomes **`BottomType`**, not the expected type, wherever the context is a plain type **[measured]**. That covers a typed local, a top-level variable, a function's body against its return type, a method's body and a typed local in it, an `if` branch, a statement, a parenthesized call, `builtinPrimitive(…)` and `fail(…)`.
   - The expected type itself is inferred only where `T` sits invariantly inside the result: `a: BoxT[\ZZ64\] = mkB()` gives `T = ZZ64`.
   - An argument to a typed parameter, an untyped binding, a loose juxtaposition, and an operand of an operator keep the stock error.
   - A method invocation today does the same: `x: ZZ64 = Fac.make()` binds `BottomType` on the stock checker.
   - The stock checker reports "Could not infer static argument T without context" at every one of these under walk's setting and under `any`. Under the compile path's setting (bound `Object`), it already gives `BottomType` everywhere, context or not.
3. **The distance** (DistanceMulti, the twelve components, the unchanged library copy L0) **[measured]**:
   - Under walk's setting: 1,737 → **1,387** (−350).
   - Under `any`: 1,746 → **1,395** (−351).
   - What went, under both settings: all 340 N1, 10 of the 24 N2, and variation in O1 (2 under walk, 2 under `any`).
   - No new error by site, except O1's known variation: 2 under walk, 1 under `any`.
   - Seven errors changed their message at their own site (I2 4, RG 2, OT 1). In each the same obligation is now refused inside the call's inference rather than at the declaration's return check.
   - Every class count except N1, N2 and O1 is unchanged. The eight declaration crashes are unchanged, and so is the `Stream` variance crash under `any`.
4. **The compiler's tests** **[measured]**: the compiler's type checker was run over all 382 `.fss` files that the gate's `.test` files `compile` or `link`, stock and shadow.
   - **No file's diagnostics differ.** 469 errors in each run, and 234 files with a non-zero return code in each.
   - The shadow's path is exercised: 1,127 distinct `f(x)` sites were given an expected type, 701 of them in `compiler_tests/`, and 14 of those inferred static arguments.
5. **What else it changes** **[measured on small programs]**:
   - Inference solves "range <: context" by subtyping and never by coercion. So a call that the stock checker accepts, because it converts the call's result afterwards, is now refused. Six of `DArg`'s 12 calls are refused this way:
     - `a: ZZ64 = idt(3)`
     - `r: RR64 = idt(3)`
     - `(): ZZ64 = idt(3)`
     - `(): ZZ64 = idt(z)` with `z: ZZ32`
     - `pick(l, 3)`
     - `inc(5)` into `ZZ64`
   - The same happens under the compiler's own library: `k03(): ZZ64 = idt(z)` (`DComp`).

## 4. The plan, in order

Units as the record's: a rung 3 to 5 agents and 1M to 2M tokens; a batch's tail 8 agents and 2M; a worker session 0.4M to 0.8M.

1. **Batch 7, widened** (H, A, and a small library rung N7): H and A as planned; N7 writes `extends Object` on `builtinPrimitive`'s and `fail`'s result parameter and takes row 421's four lines out of rung L; question 1 of batch 7 at its default (a), the bound `Any`. With A's 307 and H's 40 by the briefs, about 890 remain; about 850 if H's families by reading go too. Needs no decision beyond batch 7's go and decision 2 below. Cost: one run of three rungs.
2. **Two worker sessions beside it, no batch** (a third, the ranges shadow, is done: measurement C, tree 2). (b) The checker shadow for the rule: a coercion retry after inference, on the Fable plan's one-shape probes and the A0 library copy; it gives batch N its shape and count before its brief (Pavol's rule of 2026-09-22). (c) Decision D's diff: the sized signatures of C4's vocabulary, measured by the microGPT driver against its 15 errors, shown to Pavol, parked for phase 5.
3. **The ranges batch**, on decision 1: `RangeInternals` and the range operators over `ZZ32` (the shadow `z32.py` is the sketch: 113 declarations lose their integer parameter, 892 written argument lists shorten, the three point operators split into the three shapes `#` and `:` already have; the public range traits stay generic in their index type), the `GeneratorZZ32` crash fixed in Java beside it, the specification's ranges section and the revival's callout at `basic-integers.tex:61-65` revised in the S1 form, its two `ZZ64` examples (`Generators.GeneratorDefn`, `Expr.Do.mySum`) and `ZZ`'s factorial property respelled or marked, the three `XXX` range tests of rows 450-452 and `RangePrototype` restated. Clears about 190 measured, 37 more once the crash is fixed (inferred), and takes every range out of the numeral switch's way. Cost: a library rung with a small Java piece, and a specification rung, one run.
4. **Batch N, the rule and the numeral**, four rungs: N-check (Scala: inference with coercion and the promotion rule; the expected type kept at `f(x)`, measured at four tokens and 350 errors by measurement D, with a retry without it so that a binding's coercion still applies, since the kept context alone refuses `a: ZZ64 = idt(3)`), N-walk (Java: the same rule in `EvaluatorBase`, `OverloadedFunction`, `Coercions`), N-lib (the sibling `IntLiteral` with its coercions in the one library, walk's `FIntLiteral.make` giving a numeral that type, the library's numeral sites respelled), N-spec (the type-inference chapter written, S1 form, landing only with N-check). Closes rows 79, 388, 389, 401, 425, 432, 443, 447, 437 and the numeral half of 426; retires batch 6.5's Q1. Its count on the library is small once steps 1 and 3 have landed; its value is the decision it lands and the programs it protects. Cost: one run of four, with a Scala and a Java rung as batches 3.5, 4 and 5 ran.
5. **Batch 7b** (S, C, W, L) as drafted, L without row 421 and without the `CAP` family if decision 1 is yes. After N because W and N-walk both edit `OverloadedFunction.java`.

## 5. Batches 6.5, 7 and 7b, rung by rung

- 6.5 E: keep; clears 0; a corner, correct and decided. Pavol's "64-bit integers" is `NatRtBigSize`'s sizes, which E restates.

## 6. Decisions for Pavol

### Decision 1. Ranges over `ZZ32` alone

- The question: make the library's scalar ranges monomorphic over `ZZ32`, as the compiler library declares them (`CompilerLibrary.fsi:173-174`), instead of generic over an integer type `I`?
- Context: the specification's ranges chapter names no width ("integer values", `ranges.tex:43-44`), but two of its own examples build `ZZ64` ranges and one property a `ZZ` range (measurement C, section 3, items 5 to 7); the compiler library's `ZZ32` ranges are the implementers' later practice; a size is an `NN32` and a JVM index a `ZZ32` (POSITIONS 2026-09-27); `RangeInternals` carries 411 of the 1,738 errors; measured, ranges over `ZZ32` clear about 190 of them and hide 37 more behind a crash that a Java line fixes, after the cheap fixes have taken theirs (tree 2: 1,239 to 1,012); in the whole tree 7 lines build a range over another width, 5 in three `XXX` interpreter tests of rows 450-452 and 2 in the specification's examples, none in the library, the demos or microGPT; the copy loads under walk and passes the range tests, and refuses `RangePrototype`, which is written generic; the language cannot convert a numeral into a type known only as `I` (both plans, evidence B section 8). Peers: Java's `IntStream.range`/`LongStream.range`, Kotlin's `IntRange`/`LongRange`, Scala's `Range` over `Int` with `NumericRange` beside it, Rust generic over any integer.
- Options: (1) yes, one library rung with the crash's Java line and one specification rung; (2) keep the generic ranges and repair them with the library's devices (85 measured, then the numeral rule or about 130 sites for the 160 numerals, then the slips one by one); (3) two concrete families, `ZZ32` and `ZZ64`, twice the range code and no generic code.

A no costs option 2's sites and makes the rule a condition of every numeral range.
- Recommended: 1. The lever is smaller than either plan guessed and still the largest numeric one on the table, and it is the compiler library's own practice.

### Decision 2. Batch 7 widened, question 1 at the bound `Any`

- The question: add rung N7 (the two written bounds, row 421's four lines) to batch 7, and take its question 1 at (a)?
- Context: measured on one copy, 1,738 to 1,239 (the bounds 363 of it, row 421 52, row 358 and the device 85); the bound `Object` on `builtinPrimitive`'s `T` makes the checker bind `Bottom` and pass the body, which is what the compile path's own setting already does to these natives; the natives' bodies are replaced at the switch-over (row 309). Under (a) the 372 `Object` errors go and the 364 natives' errors come, which N7 then clears. The one `N2` left is not result-only (the tuple comparisons' `opr <[\A,B\]`). The checker's own fix (measurement D) clears the same 340 by the same `Bottom` and refuses six probe calls that convert their result today, so it is batch N's and the written bounds are batch 7's; the bounds go with the natives' bodies at the switch-over.
- Options: (1) yes; (2) batch 7 as drafted, the 400 left until the switch-over.
- A yes commits him to one more small library rung in the next run. A no costs nothing now and 400 errors on the count until the natives are rebound.
- Recommended: 1.

### Decision 3. The rule and the numeral switch as one batch, before 7b

- The question: build inference with coercion, the promotion rule and the expected type at `f(x)` on both paths, with the numeral switch and the type-inference chapter, as batch N right after the ranges batch and before 7b?
- Context: the switch he decided cannot land alone (13 and 11 refused declarations measured; row 401's shape behind decision D's errors); the rule is answer 8's, placed "in the checker phase" by the plan's batching, not by him; on the count it is small after steps 1 and 3; 7b's W and N-walk share a file, so the two are sequential either way.
- Options: (1) N before 7b, as section 4; (2) N after 7b, the coordinator's order; (3) N folded into 7b as four larger rungs, one run of 9 to 15 hours.
- A yes to 1 retires the numeral decision and 6.5's Q1 one batch sooner, and writes the inference chapter before S rewrites the overloading passages that cite it; a no (option 2) costs nothing on the count and delays the switch by one run.
- Recommended: 1; option 2 is acceptable if the checker shadow (2b) is not ready when the ranges batch lands.

### Decision 4. Decision D's diff now

- The question: one worker session now for the sized signatures of C4's vocabulary, shown to him as a diff, parked until phase 5?
- Context: 15 of each program's visible errors are the unsized `Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]` meeting sized library declarations; the array design review predicted it; the diff was wanted "as soon as step 3 lands" by the library-route judgement and is held in phase 5.
- Options: (1) yes; (2) wait for phase 5.
- A yes costs one session and buys the shape of microGPT's own gate before the switch-over is designed. A no costs nothing now.
- Recommended: 1.

### Decision 5. The order

- The question: 7 widened, the ranges batch, N, 7b, 8, with 6.5 in the slots a decision leaves (G first)?
- Options: (1) that order; (2) the record's: 6.5, 7, 7b, then the rest; (3) the coordinator's: 7 widened, ranges, 7b, N, 8, 6.5 in the slots.

- Recommended: 1.

# The C series and the APL side quest: state and what comes next

## Where the work stands

The goal is to finish what the designers intended, judged by the latest committed specification (`Specification/`, the July 2012 draft), not to redesign the language, with one program as the measuring stick: microGPT, compiled to bytecode and running fast (the root `CLAUDE.md` § Project goal; `coordinator/POSITIONS.md`, 2026-09-16).

The live thread is the one library. The interpreter's library (`FortressLibrary` and `FortressBuiltin`) is to become the library the compiler checks, and the work is to bring the compiled checker to accept it (`coordinator/POSITIONS.md`, 2026-09-21). Between that library and bytecode stands the checker, not desugaring or code generation; it reports 62 errors on the library since climb batch 6's rung F flattened the number tower (`FortressBuiltin` 18 to 0, `FortressLibrary` 110 to 38, `RangeInternals` 78 to 42, `NativeArray`'s 44 unchanged), 125 from climb batch 4 through batch 5, 103 before it (rung N's declared rise: the 22 `fill` overloading errors in `NativeArray` that the crash it removed had hidden; `compile-ladder/climb-batch-4/RECORD.md`, "The merged-diff review"), and the table of climb batch 6b's landing, `compile-ladder/climb-batch-6b/gate/checker-count.txt`, the same 62 and identical to that of rung R's follow-up to batch 6, is the next batch's comparand. Since `a2b4809a5` (2026-09-23) the count is reported and never red on its own, because a fix can raise it; the gate stays red on a crash line no rung declared, a stale shadow or a table with no total (`coordinator/FACTS.md` § The checker and the one library; `coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.md`, the checker count). The route on the checker's multiple instantiation exclusion, the rule that no type may be two different instantiations of one generic, which 61 of batch 5's 125 errors came from, is decided, and climb batch 6's rung F carried it out on the one library (`coordinator/FACTS.md`, "The one library's number tower is flat"): route A, the rule kept and the library's numeric tower flattened, with the interpreter taught coercion first (`coordinator/POSITIONS.md`, 2026-09-24; the brief `reviews/exclusion-design-brief.md`; route C measured whole in `reviews/mie-probes/route-c-experiment.md`). How a `nat` size is carried at run time is decided too: design B, a size given the same descriptor object a type argument has, filling the slot the code generator already reserves (`coordinator/POSITIONS.md`, 2026-09-24; `reviews/size-runtime-design-brief.md`, revised after the three size probes and the cost measurement, `perf-probes/nat/size-probes.md`, `size-cost.md`). The two probes that precede the run-time size rung's brief landed on 2026-09-25 (`perf-probes/nat/size-rung-probes.md`): a number's descriptor made by the loader on first request or by a factory with no holder class gives the same answers

Decided, in `coordinator/POSITIONS.md`: the goal and its measuring stick (2026-09-16); test first, the test written and seen failing before the fix and kept in the corpus from then on (2026-09-17); the workflow, with workers pushing to their own `wip/` branches, the script in the repository and the higher tier called only at a refusal, a stop or a red gate (2026-09-18), narrowed to a judge's second ruling on the same rung or tree (2026-09-24); unboxed `double[]` storage and the `nat` sizes taken together, as the team designed them (2026-09-19); the tier rule, workers on the cheaper tier and a worker on the top tier only with his permission (2026-09-20); one library, the interpreter's, with no new declaration in the compiler prelude and its three files deleted at the switch-over (2026-09-21); route A and design B (2026-09-24, above), and the rows batch 3.5 handed back, 379, 380/381 and 383 (2026-09-24); re-approval rows 39 and 40 (2026-09-24, 2026-09-25) and 47 (2026-09-26). What comes next is the plan Pavol approved on 2026-09-26, `coordinator/PLAN.md` (`coordinator/POSITIONS.md`, 2026-09-26, the plan): its six phases from batch 5 to microGPT running fast, his answers in the order they are needed, the four workers sent out that day (W1-W4) and the parked items are there and are not repeated here. \Trait{Fortress.Standard.TotalComparison}

The comparison operator \OPR{CMP}, when applied to values belonging
to a total order, typically returns a value of type \TYP{TotalComparison}.
The three values of type \TYP{TotalComparison} are
called \TYP{LessThan}, \TYP{EqualTo}, and \TYP{GreaterThan}.

This trait supports an associative operator \OPR{LEXICO} that
is useful for supporting lexicographic comparison of ordered sequences;
the trick is to compare the sequences elementwise and then to use the
\OPR{LEXICO} operator to reduce the sequence of comparison results.
Note that \TYP{EqualTo} is the identity for \OPR{LEXICO},
and all other comparison values are left zeroes for \OPR{LEXICO}.

If a trait declaration of \VAR{T} includes a \KWD{comprises} clause
then the traits listed in its \KWD{comprises} clause

If the \KWD{comprises} clause of a trait \VAR{T} includes ``\EXP{\ldots}''

then in a component exporting the enclosing API,
other traits may explicitly extend \VAR{T},
\(\KWD{trait} \TYP{InclusiveMolecule} \KWD{extends} \{\,\TYP{InorganicMolecule}, \TYP{OrganicMolecule}\,\} \KWD{end}\)
\end{Fortress}

For the same reason, a trait or object may not extend
two instantiations of one parameterized trait
that exclude each other by instantiation exclusion (\secref{trait-types}),
directly or through its supertraits:
any two instantiations of one parameterized trait that it extends
must have the same static arguments, operator arguments excepted.
